subject: Reconciliation: KMS responsibility + subprocessor dataflow mapping
messages:
From: Anne Li <anne.li@medihealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medihealth.com>
Date: Mon, 10 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: KMS responsibility and subprocessor dataflow mapping

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's routing/fallback features. We are starting our security review and need two clarifications before we can onboard a proof-of-concept:

1) A short mapping that explicitly shows which Redwood subprocessors have access to customer encryption keys or any plaintext data in transit at rest (KMS breakouts).
2) A dataflow diagram that highlights where tokens/KV cache and logs are stored and which third parties (if any) have direct access.

Can you share an initial artifact and the expected timeline for any redactions or NDAs needed to review full evidence (SOC 2 report, SIG attachments)? Our compliance team is preparing a narrow set of questions (I can share) but they need the above to triage scope.

Attachments: example inventory template (MediHealth standard) — we will send our template tomorrow.

Thanks,
Anne Li
Manager, Vendor Security
MediHealth Systems
From: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Anne Li <anne.li@medihealth.com>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medihealth.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Nov 2025 11:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: KMS responsibility and subprocessor dataflow mapping

Hi Anne —

Thanks for the note. I attached our first-pass subprocessor inventory and a KMS responsibility worksheet (redwood_subproc_kms_mapping_v1.xlsx). High level:

- Redwood controls customer-managed keys only in Private deployments where customers configure their KMS; in Hosted mode, encryption at rest is managed by our cloud provider and customer data encryption keys are envelope-encrypted by Redwood-managed KMS (we call this "Redwood-managed KMS").
- Subprocessors that may handle plaintext or caching during inference (short-lived KV cache) are: inference-gpu-pool (logging & cache eviction service), tokenizer-service (transient plaintext for tokenization), and metrics-collector (aggregated, pseudonymized metrics).
- None of our analytics partners receive plaintext tokens; metrics are aggregated. We mark fields in the spreadsheet where we believe MediHealth will want stronger controls.

Please note the attached is redacted for vendor contacts. If you need contact-level evidence (e.g., SOC or a vendor contract excerpt), let me know and we can route through our legal/compliance team. Timeline: we can provide a more detailed zone-by-zone diagram and SOC 2 summary by Friday (14 Nov) after a quick internal sync.

Quick question: do you need absolute proof of KMS key handling at the HSM level (i.e., certificate/KMS audit events), or is a scoped statement of responsibility and keyflow sufficient for your vendor team to triage?

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_subproc_kms_mapping_v1.xlsx; subprocessor_inventory_snapshot_20251110.csv
From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 12 Nov 2025 09:30:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request: KMS responsibility and subprocessor dataflow mapping

Sofia — forwarding Anne's request and your draft. A couple notes from infra: we do not export HSM audit logs to subprocessors; KMS audit events live in our logging cluster (retention 90 days by default, configurable per-customer on Dedicated/Private). Clarifications to include in the next revision:

- Explicitly state retention windows for KV cache (default 30s-5m depending on model) and how that differs between Hosted and Dedicated.
- Call out which components run in customer VPC for Private deployments (agent, local cache) vs Redwood-managed clusters.
- For Hosted customers we have an option to rotate envelope keys per-customer every N days; include the rotation cadence and whether we share rotation proof with customers.

I'll draft suggested language and send a tracked changes copy by EOD Thursday. If legal needs to step in for SOC redaction or NDA coordination, loop in Kimberly.

— Logan
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Anne Li <anne.li@medihealth.com>
To: sofia_ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
Cc: Tom Reynolds <tom.reynolds@medihealth.com>, security@medihealth.com
Date: Fri, 14 Nov 2025 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request: KMS responsibility and subprocessor dataflow mapping

Sofia, Logan —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and the worksheet. The MediHealth vendor team reviewed the spreadsheet and has three asks before we can move to a POC:

1) Can you confirm the KV cache default retention and provide the configuration knobs for Dedicated vs Hosted (we'd like to ensure Hosted default is within our risk tolerance).
2) Please provide a redacted SOC 2 summary that includes control mappings for key management and physical/logical access to KMS (we don't need the full report yet).
3) We'll need a short mutual NDA so we can exchange vendor-level SOC attachments and vendor contracts — can you send a DocuSign link or point of contact in legal?

If you can provide items 1–3 by COB Monday (17 Nov) that would work for our timeline. Also, if there's an internal matrix that maps subprocessors to specific control IDs (SIG or CAIQ rows), that would be very helpful.

Thanks — I'll follow up with a short questionnaire later today.

Best,
Anne Li
Manager, Vendor Security
MediHealth Systems

short_summary: External vendor (MediHealth) requested KMS responsibility mapping and subprocessor dataflow. Sofia provided initial redacted inventory; infra clarified retention and Hosted vs Private differences. MediHealth requested KV retention values, SOC 2 summary, and an NDA to proceed with POC.
